morphemes.formRelation: direct
TRACT reflects the tract- form seen in Latin tractum; not a standalone Latin lemma.
DUC follows the verbal base; DUCT reflects the duct- form seen in Latin ductum.
SCRIPT reflects the script- form; Allen & Greenough documents the phonetic development scriptus from an earlier scrib-tus sequence.
MIT follows the present stem family; MISS reflects the miss- form visible in Latin missum.
CAP follows the verbal base; CAPT reflects the capt- form seen in Latin captum. CEPT/CEIV are not asserted here because they require a separate Romance/English historical derivation layer.
PRAE- is the attested Latin form from prae. English PRE- is a downstream historical reflex and is intentionally not asserted by the source-language authority layer.

morphemes.formRelation: Variant behavior follows Latin phonology.
Allen & Greenough lists de- in compounds with the adverbial values down / utterly.
Assimilation may occur in compounds, but no learner-facing variant is published here until each form is explicitly represented and tested.
FIN is the pedagogical form tied to Latin finis; downstream English-word membership must be verified separately.
PEND is tied to the Latin pendeo family; downstream English-word membership is a separate claim.
Allen & Greenough lists ante- as a verbal prefix retaining the adverbial sense BEFORE.
Allen & Greenough lists circum- with the adverbial sense AROUND.
Allen & Greenough lists super- with the senses UPON / OVER AND ABOVE.
Allen & Greenough treats dis-/di- as an inseparable particle with the senses ASUNDER / APART.
Allen & Greenough lists red-/re- as an inseparable particle with the senses BACK / AGAIN.
Allen & Greenough lists sed-/se- as an inseparable particle with the sense APART.
LSJ explicitly records αὐτός in compound use with the value self-/of or by oneself.
LSJ explicitly describes σύν in composition as with / along with / together and as marking union or connection.
Smyth explicitly identifies root γραφ and gives λογο-γράφο-ς as a compound; GRAPH is the conventional Latin-letter teaching transliteration of γραφ-.

stemDerivation.method: explicit root in Smyth; compound evidence in λογο-γράφο-ς

morphemes.formRelation: Smyth explicitly gives λογο- as the stem of λόγος and λογο-γράφο-ς as a compound; LOG/LOGO represent that attested stem family.

stemDerivation.method: explicit noun stem in Smyth and compound λογο-γράφο-ς

morphemes.formRelation: βίος is a second-declension noun; Smyth defines the second declension as O-stems, supporting βιο- as the source stem. BIO is the Latin-letter teaching transliteration of βιο-.

stemDerivation.method: second-declension O-stem rule applied to attested βίος

morphemes.formRelation: LSJ attests γεω- in γεωγραφέω 'describe the earth's surface'; GEO is therefore tied to an attested Greek compound form, not inferred from English spelling.

stemDerivation.method: attested compound form γεω- in LSJ γεωγραφέω

morphemes.formRelation: LSJ identifies ἄφωνος as formed from φωνή, directly exposing φων- in composition. PHON is the Latin-letter teaching transliteration of that attested compound stem.

stemDerivation.method: attested compound form in LSJ ἄφωνος (from φωνή)

morphemes.formRelation: Allen & Greenough §267 lists a/ab as verbal prefixes retaining the adverbial sense AWAY.
Allen & Greenough §267 lists amb- with am-/an- variants and the sense AROUND.
Allen & Greenough §267 lists por- as an inseparable particle with the sense FORWARD.
Allen & Greenough §267d explicitly treats per- as an adverbial intensive prefix meaning VERY. This record does not cover prepositional per 'through'.
LSJ gives the radical sense THROUGH and attests διά as a productive prepositional element; DIA- is its Latin-letter teaching form.
LSJ attests μετά with genitive/dative senses around WITH/AMONG and accusative AFTER. Downstream English senses such as 'meta-' = self-referential are not owned by this authority record.
LSJ explicitly describes παρά in compounds with beside/alongside, past, and beyond/amiss relations.
LSJ gives περί the core spatial sense AROUND / ROUND ABOUT; PERI- is the Latin-letter teaching form.
LSJ explicitly treats πρό in compounds with BEFORE/FORWARDS and related senses. This Greek PRO- record is distinct from Latin pro-.
LSJ explicitly states that ὑπέρ signifies OVER/ABOVE and documents compound uses including excess beyond measure.
LSJ gives ὑπό the core spatial senses UNDER / FROM UNDER; HYPO- is the Latin-letter teaching form.

Lewis & Short explicitly derives dictio from dico and defines it as saying/speaking/uttering. DICT is kept as a conservative teaching form tied to the attested dictio family; the fuller DIC/DICT verbal alternation belongs to a later audited expansion.
FAC follows the facio family; FACT reflects the fact- form in attested Latin factum. English FECT/FIC reflexes are intentionally not asserted by this source-language layer.
FER follows the present/infinite family of Latin fero/ferre. The irregular perfect tuli and supine latum are retained as source forms but are not collapsed into a single English teaching root.
MOV follows the moveo/movi family; MOT reflects the mot- form in Latin motum.
PON follows the present family of pono; POSIT reflects the posit- form in Latin positum. English POS- is not separately asserted here without a downstream historical mapping.
PORT is directly tied to the Latin porto/portare family.
RUPT reflects the rupt- form in attested Latin ruptum; Lewis & Short explicitly gives the root rup and the break/burst/tear sense family.
SENT follows the present family of sentio; SENS reflects the sens- form visible in sensi/sensum.

Lewis & Short defines spectio as an observing and explicitly derives it from specio. SPECT is published conservatively from the attested spectio family; SPEC is withheld until the underlying verbal stem chain is separately sourced.
STRUCT reflects the struct- form in Latin structum; Lewis & Short gives struo with the meanings place upon one another, pile up, arrange, build.
TEN follows the present family of teneo; TENT reflects the tent- form in Latin tentum. English TAIN is a later historical reflex and is not asserted here.
VEN follows the present family of venio; VENT reflects the vent- form in Latin ventum.
VOC is directly tied to the Latin voco/vocare family. English VOK spellings are not source-language forms and are excluded.
VID follows the video/vidi family; VIS reflects the vis- form in Latin visum.
FORM is directly preserved in Latin formo/formare. Lewis & Short defines formo as to shape, fashion, form.
GRAD is visible in gradior; GRESS is the attested participial/perfect-family form gressus.
Lewis & Short explicitly identifies root sta- for sto; STAT reflects the stat- form in Latin statum.
CED is visible in cedo; CESS reflects the cess- forms cessi/cessum. English CEED is intentionally excluded from this Latin authority layer.
Lewis & Short records cludo as a frequent compound form of claudo and clausi/clausum as the closed-form family; CLUD/CLUS are therefore source-language grounded.
CURR is visible in curro; CURS reflects the curs- form in Latin cursum.
Lewis & Short explicitly marks root gen- under gigno, so GEN is not inferred from English spelling.
VIV is directly grounded in Latin vivo. VIT is not asserted here because it belongs to the separate vita/historical-derivation path.
VITA is the attested Latin noun vita 'life'. The shortened English teaching form VIT is intentionally withheld until a downstream historical mapping is sourced.
